approved: International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Amendment Bill 2013

The International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Amendment Bill 2013 was moved to bring the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Criminal Court within the scope of the act, enabling regulations to confer privileges and immunities. The Not-for-profit Sector Freedom to Advocate Bill 2013 was proposed to prohibit and invalidate clauses in Commonwealth agreements that restrict not-for-profit entities from advocating on Commonwealth policy issues.

Moved a bill to bring the International Committee of the Red Cross and the International Criminal Court within the International Organisations (Privileges and Immunities) Act 1963, enabling regulations to confer legal personality and immunities under a 2005 headquarters agreement with the ICRC and paving the way for Australia's accession to the ICC's privileges and immunities agreement.

Supported the bill extending privileges and immunities to the ICRC and International Criminal Court, noting the ICRC delivered food to 617,000 people and water to 100,000 people in Syria between January and March this year, and recalled the Howard government's 2002 ratification of the Rome Statute following an 18-month inquiry that received more than 250 submissions.
